rows.title: webtools-http: outbound-URL policies `Trusted`/`Untrusted`, `TransportSettings` and the common address classifier
rows.detail: Merged through PR #86 as 53965c8: the outbound-URL policies, `TransportSettings`, `CidrBlock`, `MixedAnswers` and the `WebToolsDsl` marker in `webtools-http`, over the internal classifier and JVM guards, with the README row; no deviation from the plan; no version moved, and `webtools-http` 1.0.0 stays unreleased.

qa.note: Every plan item and acceptance criterion traced to the code, the public surface exactly the planned Stable Core set, hygiene clean. The findings, all minor: the internal JVM guards (`GuardedDns`, `GuardedSocket`, `GuardedSocketFactory`, `PolicyEnforcement`, the markers) lacked contract tags and the facts a wirer needs (builder wiring, thread, the `DEBUG` line, guard order, the stackless markers); the common helpers (`OutboundUrlPolicy.kt`, `UrlGuard`, `StrictIp`, the test support) carried line comments where KDoc is due; six bit-arithmetic or reserved-name lines (`CidrBlock`, `AddressRanges`, `HostRules`, `UrlGuard`) lacked a comment; one duplicated assertion (`TrustedGuardComponentTest`), one timing bound equal to its timeout (`PolicyEnforcementOkHttpIntegrationTest`) and two dangling cross-references in the as-built record.

Pass 1's fixes confirmed with no regression, and stage S8 checked line for line against the plan: the `WebToolsDsl` marker, the six builders that carry it, both of its tests and the dump's three new lines, with no JavaScript warning once plan Amendment 5 left the retention at its default. Correctness clean and every acceptance criterion met. The findings: KDoc tags on the sibling test fixtures, a boundary paragraph on `GuardedSocket`, four line comments, stale S8 wording in the records, the host-form count reconciled to the 36 forms the parent research's table publishes, and pre-existing wording in the documents the commits carry that states each unit's sizing. 504 tests in 90 classes passed, the change's 36 classes (232 tests) among them.

Code review passed: the deadline seam is inert at its defaults, the public factory and the ABI dump are unchanged, and every moved assertion is preserved; one plan-bookkeeping note (the §9 tables and Acceptance 2 still name the pre-move test homes) goes to the plan's reconciliation. All four pass-1 findings verified answered. Two minor test findings, both in the As built rows the fixes touch, fixed on the spot: the fixture `webtoolsUrl`'s three refusal branches have no test (a `WebtoolsUrlComponentTest` is added); `receiveHeaders`' four pure table cases sit at Level 2 rather than 4a (moved, for consistency with pass 1). qa.note: Code review passed: the implementation is the plan's design as written, the ABI diff is additions only, and all six acceptance criteria are met. Seven test findings, in the As built rows the fixes touch: two uncovered defensive branches in CaffeineResponseCache, each wanting one Level 2 method (`close`: a foreign cancellation of the shared future read as closed; `failure-value`: an Error thrown by the load dispatcher mapped to fatal); six runBlocking methods in LoaderRunnerComponentTest to move under runTest and one test name to reword (`component-tests`); two Level 4a table rows for CacheExpiry and CacheEntry.isFailure (`deterministic-tests`); and the P5 procedure and an acceptance mapping missing from the as-built record (`release`, whose verdict names P5). Suite: 883 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

Test audit: compliant at every level, and all seven remediations from pass 1 hold. Code review: one minor finding, in the As built row the fix touches (`caffeine-default`, whose verdict logs `DEBUG` once per load end): the load body logs its "load ended" line before knowing whether its completion won, so a result a mid-flight `close()` or `invalidate(key)` discards still reads `stored`, and after `close()` a second line follows, against the once-per-load-end rule (plan.md R12, §6.9). The fix logs the line only when the completion wins. Suite: 887 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.

rows.title: webtools-http: `CallBudget` port, `WindowedCallBudget`, rate signals, the persistence and observer seams and their fakes
rows.detail: Landed in PR #90.

qa.note: One code finding (other), in the As built row the fix touches, `hard-stop`, whose verdict holds the write-ahead and the snapshots (plan.md R13, §6.7): in `BudgetLedger`'s `exactSnapshot` and `markPersisted`, after a write-ahead grant is released and `flush()` runs, the exact snapshot omits the emptied hard cell while its persisted mark keeps the write-ahead value, so up to `persistAhead - 1` later grants make no save and a crash under-counts the hard window, against the plan's never-under-count rule; the code is the plan's own, so the fix is also a deviation. Two minor test findings, in `component-tests`, each a Level 2 case to add: the write-ahead retry loop is exercised only for its first iteration (no slow successful save crossing a boundary, no three-attempt cap case), and the 1 ms re-plan deadline tolerance has no edge case. Suite: 1,204 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. For the documents: the Level 2 close test with free capacity appears to detect P3's mutation deterministically, to be confirmed with one run; P5 has no record yet.

Five minor findings and no other; the fixes are being made in place. Two in the As built row `fixtures`: the code finding, that `FakeBudgetStore`'s `failLoads` and `failSaves` with `times = 0` deliver one failure instead of none, because the count only decides when to disarm and the armed failure is still delivered; a guard settles it, with a case of its own, and as the code is the plan's listing (plan.md §7.17) the fix is also a deviation. And a test finding: `FixturesConsumerGatingTest` names neither `RecordingBudgetObserver` nor `FakeBudgetStore`. The other three are test findings in `component-tests`, each a case to add, resting on another row's verdict: for `close`, a waiter whose own write-ahead save spans `close()`; for `hard-stop`, a store `Error` propagating (plan.md §6.7) and a retried restore whose merge of counts re-plans queued waiters. Looked at with no finding: the D7 fix, a single added condition traced through every snapshot reader, and the restore band, which is plan.md §6.7's contract. Suite: 1,208 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
